newsitem.title: USA: Gulfport, Mississippi to open air cargo center.
newsitem.headline: Gulfport, Mississippi to open air cargo center.

text.p: The Gulfport-Biloxi Regional Airport in Mississippi is building an air cargo centre and hopes to lure some Latin American cargo business from Miami International Airport, the centre's operator said Tuesday.
"It is a perfect place for a new gateway to Latin America. It is much closer to the heartland of America than Miami," John Wilkes, president of Americas Cargo Enterprises, told Reuters.
The Pascagoula, Miss.-based Americas Cargo will operate the cargo centre.
"We think we'll find a great niche with Latin America," airport director Bruce Frallic said. "We already do a lot of trade with Central and South America."
The seaport at Gulfport is the largest port for bananas in the United States and the largest port for the export of frozen chicken, Frallic said.
Currently the airport has 36 scheduled flights a day, but none is international, Frallic said.

The airport broke ground on the new cargo centre in December and hopes to have it open in May or June, Wilkes said. The first phase is a 15,000-square-foot building with 2,000 square feet of cooler space, Wilkes said. The building has ramp access and four truck docks.
"There is plenty of room to expand," Wilkes said.
So far no firm contracts have been signed but both executives said they are negotiating with several potential users of the building.
"We see this as an alternative for Miami," Wilkes said.
"Latin American cargo is growing so rapidly. We could have a nice little business here and Miami wouldn't miss it." -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
